title: the-chart-contract-is-the-chain-tools
intention: The chart chain's contract, which codemother's verdict and stage machines happen to hold, moves down a rung into the chain tool: the verdict coverage reader (unanswered, falsifier_criteria, FALSIFIER_REF, VerdictRefused) and the verdict-deposit ledger (LEDGER_PATH, read_ledger, pending, enqueue_verdict, mark_deposited) go to a new module cairn/tools/chain/verdict_contract.py, and every stage's authored-field tuple goes to one table STAGE_AUTHORED_FIELDS in cairn/tools/chain/grammar.py. The build inspector, the PROVED crossing in transitions, the two tools/base probes and the chart dial read them from the chain tool, so no gate and no dial reaches into codemother. Codemother's machines bind the same objects from the chain tool, so behaviour is unchanged.
why: RULE 1 child: the build inspector, the PROVED crossing, two probes and the chart dial reach into codemother's machines for the chart contract; the contract is chart's and moves down a rung to the chain tool
traces_to: RULE 1 (encapsulation — a component reaches another only through its declared public interface; a device's is the bus) via parent 8e3474a6ae43; Law 1 (one table of stage fields, not seven tuples and a dial restating them); Law 6 (chart owns the ledger — verdict.py's own comment — and the chain tool is chart's shared contract); Law 8 (the PROVED gate's coverage check is unchanged in behaviour).
how: Measured 2026-10-02 (encapsulation_breaches(Path('.').resolve()) from cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py): 166 rows, 48 landing in cairn/devices/codemother. This ticket clears the rows whose target is the contract rather than codemother acting: cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py:58 (claiming_packets, unanswered, verdict_error — the first and last already live in cairn/tools/chain/chain.py and verdict.py only re-exports them), cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:1693 (enqueue_verdict, at the PROVED crossing), cairn/tools/base/probes/no_component_reaches_proved_with_an_uncharted_build.py:48 and unchartered_build_edits.py:56 (chain_for_ticket, also already in chain.py), cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_transitions.py:766 (patches the enqueue's module globals) and :876 (asserts the import string), cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector_nexus.py:205-206 (asks the dynamic-import question of orient and verdict as members of the inspector's closure; after the move the closure member is the chain tool, so it asks verdict_contract), cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs_disabled/test_probe.py:31,318, and skills/chart/dial.py:31-38 (seven imports for AUTHORED_FIELDS only). The moved code is verdict.py lines 99-307 (FALSIFIER_REF, _CLAUSE_RE, VerdictRefused, falsifier_criteria, _read_falsifier_chain, _read_chain, unanswered) and 747-857 (the ledger, whose own comment reads 'Law 6: chart owns the ledger'); its only imports are json, os, re, time and cairn.tools.chain (grammar.ticket_path, CAIRN_ROOT, INSTANCE_DIR; chain.latest_claiming_artifact). verdict.py imports the moved names back from the chain tool so codemother's write_verdict and skills/chart/live.py keep working by identity. Each of the seven stage machines sets AUTHORED_FIELDS = STAGE_AUTHORED_FIELDS['<stage>'] (values unchanged). The chain tool's charter gains cairn.tools.chain.verdict_contract in public_interface. Not this ticket's: skills/chart/live.py's 25 rows (codemother depositing a berthed packet is codemother acting, so it becomes a bus verb, sibling the-chart-deposit-is-a-codemother-verb); cairn/tools/tree/proofs/test_chart_tree.py's orient tests, cairn/tools/bus_client and cairn/tools/operator_inbox proofs and probes reaching codemother (sibling codemothers-proof-halves-move-home).
